input.quote: 15.9 Governing Law. The construction and validity of this Agreement and the provisions hereof, and the rights and obligations of the Parties hereunder, will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA, and, to the extent applicable to Patents and Trademarks, the applicable federal laws of the USA, in each instance without regard to conflict of laws principles.
input.rationale: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware or California law) rather than the preferred New York choice, so it is acceptable and not redlined. On forum, Section 15.10 requires Executive Officer escalation and then final and binding ICDR arbitration, but the seat is New York and the arbitration is governed by the Federal Arbitration Act (Section 15.10.2.2), so there is no foreign seat and no exclusive foreign venue in SFJ's home jurisdiction — the walk-away trigger is not met. The clause also preserves U.S. federal court determination of IP ownership/validity disputes and either Party's right to seek preliminary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction. The only shortfalls versus the preferred position are the Delaware (rather than New York) law and the use of domestic arbitration instead of New York County courts; both are noted rather than flagged.
